newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CHELSEA FAIL IN BID FOR MALDINI.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHELSEA FAIL IN BID FOR MALDINI.

text.p: English premier league side Chelsea tried to bring Italy defender Paolo Maldini to London but were put off by AC Milan's "ridiculous" asking price, player-manager Ruud Gullit said on Friday.
"I heard the rumours that Milan were ready to sell a whole lot of players and I wouldn't be doing my job well if I didn't ask for Maldini," Gullit said.

"They asked me if I was interested...and as a coach you'd be crazy not to be interested in him. But I don't think I'm going to get him because they are asking for something ridiculous. I can't imagine Milan will sell him but I had to ask.

"If I could get Maldini for a good price I would snap him up but they were asking an extremely high figure," said Gullit, who has already plundered serie A to bring Gianluca Vialli, Roberto Di Matteo and Gianfranco Zola to Stamford Bridge.
Chelsea were rumoured on Tuesday to have made enquiries about the Italian captain only to rebuffed by Milan's 17 million pound ($28 million) asking price.
Gullit also said Chelsea would play a prestigious friendly against his former club on February 19.
"It's a big compliment for the club to be invited to play a club like Milan. It will be a great experience for the youngsters to play in a stadium like the San Siro. It will give them a boost."
